candidates.title: CSV output for review
candidates.body:
## What

Add `--format csv` to `aos review`, with the columns rank, score, level, rule id, identity, message and fix, so reviewers can open the findings in a spreadsheet.

## Where to look

- `src/agent_off_switch/cli.py` (the `review` subparser lists the formats; `inventory` already has a `csv` choice to copy)
- `src/agent_off_switch/review.py` (add `to_csv(inv, found)` next to `to_markdown` and `to_json`; `Finding` has `rule_id`, `identity`, `score`, `level`, `message`, `fix`)
- `src/agent_off_switch/inventory.py` (`to_csv` is the pattern: `csv.DictWriter`, `lineterminator="\n"`)
- `tests/test_review.py`

## Acceptance criteria

- `aos review examples/demo-tenant --format csv` prints a header row plus one row per finding, highest score first, rank starting at 1.
- Test: the row count equals the finding count.
- Test: a message holding a comma and a quote survives a round trip through `csv.reader`.
- The README or docs list the new format wherever the review formats are listed.

Everything runs offline: build inputs inside the test with the helpers in `tests/conftest.py` (`demo_inv` is the demo tenant), and try the result on `examples/demo-tenant/`.

Setup and checks are in CONTRIBUTING.md: `ruff check .` and `python -m pytest -q`. Comment here to claim it; small PRs are welcome.

candidates.title: OF-03 — Data Analyst: bounded CSV profile
candidates.body:
**Labels:** `good first issue`, `department` · **Size:** small

**Scope:** Add `data_analyst` for an existing mission CSV: row count, column names, missingness, bounded unique counts and numeric min/max with explicit parsing failures.

**Targets:** `backend/app/departments/data_analyst.py` **(new)**; `backend/tests/test_data_analyst.py` **(new)**; reuse `backend/app/core/memory_vault.py`.

**Acceptance:** Use the standard-library CSV parser and sandbox read limits; enforce at most 10,000 rows/100 columns; save a machine-readable profile and Markdown report; record truncation and inferred-type uncertainty. Fixtures include quoted newlines, empty cells, malformed rows and invalid UTF-8. Never execute spreadsheet formulas or interpolate cells as instructions. No pandas dependency needed.

Source: https://github.com/MrMha/openfoundry/blob/main/docs/GOOD_FIRST_ISSUES.md

Please comment before starting so work can be coordinated. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md and include focused deterministic tests.

candidates.title: Export leads to CSV
candidates.body:
Export every lead to a CSV file, so owners can open their pipeline in a spreadsheet or back it up.

## Requirements

1. **CLI:** `python3 leadgen.py export` writes CSV to stdout, so this works:
   `python3 leadgen.py export > leads.csv`
   - Use the stdlib `csv` module. No third-party dependencies (see CONTRIBUTING.md).
   - The first row is a header. Include **every column of the `leads` table**, in table order. Read the
     columns from the database (for example `PRAGMA table_info(leads)` or `cursor.description`), not
     from a hard-coded list, so columns added later are exported too.
   - One row per lead, ordered by `id`.
   - Multi-line fields (research, pitch, brief...) must stay in one cell: let `csv.writer` quote them.
   - Show `export` in the usage text (the module docstring at the top of `leadgen.py`).
2. **Download link (optional, welcome):** a "Download CSV" link on the Leads page served at
   `GET /leads.csv`, with `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and
   `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="leads.csv"`. Build the CSV with the **same function** as
   the CLI. Don't write the logic twice.

## Security checks (required)

- `GET /leads.csv` must go through the existing `ok_origin()` check in `do_GET`, like every other route.
  Don't add a route that skips it: this file holds every lead's contact details.
- **CSV formula injection:** lead data comes from the web. Any cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`,
  a tab or a carriage return must be prefixed with a single quote `'`, so Excel or Sheets doesn't run it
  as a formula. Example: `=HYPERLINK(...)` becomes `'=HYPERLINK(...)`.
- Don't log or write the export anywhere except stdout or the HTTP response.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 leadgen.py export` prints a header plus one row per lead, with all `leads` columns.
- [ ] A lead whose notes span several lines round-trips through `csv.reader` unchanged.
- [ ] A cell starting with `=` is exported with a leading `'`.
- [ ] If the download link is added: `/leads.csv` returns 200 with a CSV attachment, and 403 when the
      `Host` header is foreign (the same check as `test_cross_site_and_rebinding_blocked`).
- [ ] No new dependencies; `leadgen.py` stays a single stdlib-only file.
- [ ] README mentions the command (CLI section) and CHANGELOG has an `Unreleased` entry.

## Testing

- Add tests to `tests/test_leadgen.py` (they use a temp DB and never call Claude). Cover:
  - the header and column set;
  - the multi-line round-trip;
  - the formula-injection prefix;
  - the `/leads.csv` 200/403 cases, if you add the route.
- Run `python3 -m unittest discover tests -v` locally. CI (ubuntu and macOS, Python 3.11 to 3.13) must
  be green on the PR.

## Out of scope

Import from CSV, filtering the export by status, and other formats (JSON, XLSX). Open a separate issue
if you want one of these.

comments.body: Hi @Hrishank21s, I am a fresher looking to make my first open-source contribution. I have experience with Python and working with CSV formats. Could you please assign this issue to me? I would love to work on it!

Hi @pragna-tummala, welcome, and thanks for offering! This issue is yours. 🎉

I've updated the issue description with the exact requirements, the security checks, the acceptance criteria and what to test, so you know precisely what "done" means.

**How to start**
1. Fork the repo and create a branch (for example `csv-export`).
2. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Hrishank21s/lead-generation-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). The key rules: stdlib only, and `leadgen.py` stays one file.
3. Implement `python3 leadgen.py export`. The `/leads.csv` download link is optional, but welcome.
4. Add tests to `tests/test_leadgen.py` and run `python3 -m unittest discover tests -v`.
5. Open a PR against `main` with `Closes #2` in the description, and fill in the PR template.

The two security points (the `ok_origin()` check and the CSV formula-injection prefix) are required, because this file holds every lead's contact details and lead data comes from the open web.

If anything is unclear, ask here. A small, focused PR is perfect for a first contribution. Looking forward to it!
